knowledge_point.title: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression

question.:question/worked-solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 3 x\operatorname{cos}(5 x)\,\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3 x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}(5 x)\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{\operatorname{sin}(5 x)}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{gathered}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3 x\cdot \operatorname{cos}(5 x)\,\text{d}x= \\ 3 x\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}(5 x)}{5}-\int \frac{\operatorname{sin}(5 x)}{5}\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{gathered}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{gathered}\int 3 x\operatorname{cos}(5 x)\,\text{d}x= \\ \frac{3 x\operatorname{sin}(5 x)}{5}-\frac{3\int \operatorname{sin}(5 x)\,\text{d}x}{5} \\ =\frac{3 x\operatorname{sin}(5 x)}{5}-\frac{3(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}(5 x)}{5})}{5}+C \\ =\frac{3 x\operatorname{sin}(5 x)}{5}+\frac{3\operatorname{cos}(5 x)}{25}+C\end{gathered}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (3 x + 5)\operatorname{sin}(x)\,\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3 x + 5\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}(x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{gathered}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (3 x + 5)\cdot \operatorname{sin}(x)\,\text{d}x= \\ (3 x + 5)\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}(x))\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{gathered}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows

$$
\begin{gathered}\int (3 x + 5)\operatorname{sin}(x)\,\text{d}x= \\ -(3 x + 5)\operatorname{cos}(x)+3\int \operatorname{cos}(x)\,\text{d}x \\ =-(3 x + 5)\operatorname{cos}(x)+3\operatorname{sin}(x)+C\end{gathered}
$$

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (6 x - 4)\operatorname{sin}(5 x)\,\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=6 x - 4\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=6 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}(5 x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}(5 x)}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{gathered}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (6 x - 4)\cdot \operatorname{sin}(5 x)\,\text{d}x= \\ (6 x - 4)\cdot (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}(5 x)}{5})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}(5 x)}{5})\cdot 6\,\text{d}x.\end{gathered}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{gathered}\int (6 x - 4)\operatorname{sin}(5 x)\,\text{d}x= \\ -\frac{(6 x - 4)\operatorname{cos}(5 x)}{5}+\frac{6\int \operatorname{cos}(5 x)\,\text{d}x}{5} \\ =-\frac{(6 x - 4)\operatorname{cos}(5 x)}{5}+\frac{6\operatorname{sin}(5 x)}{25}+C\end{gathered}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 3 x\operatorname{csc}^{2}(x + 4)\,\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3 x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{csc}^{2}(x + 4)\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cot}(x + 4).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{gathered}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3 x\cdot \operatorname{csc}^{2}(x + 4)\,\text{d}x= \\ 3 x\cdot (-\operatorname{cot}(x + 4))-\int (-\operatorname{cot}(x + 4))\cdot 3\,\text{d}x \\ =-3 x\operatorname{cot}(x + 4)+3\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}(x + 4)}{\operatorname{sin}(x + 4)}\,\text{d}x.\end{gathered}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral using the substitution $u=\operatorname{sin}(x + 4),$ where $\text{d}u=\operatorname{cos}(x + 4)\,\text{d}x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{gathered}\int 3 x\operatorname{csc}^{2}(x + 4)\,\text{d}x= \\ -3 x\operatorname{cot}(x + 4)+3\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}(x + 4)}{\operatorname{sin}(x + 4)}\,\text{d}x \\ =-3 x\operatorname{cot}(x + 4)+3\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\ =-3 x\operatorname{cot}(x + 4)+3\ln|u|+C \\ =-3 x\operatorname{cot}(x + 4)+3\ln|\operatorname{sin}(x + 4)|+C\end{gathered}
$$
